selected.rationale: Network loss between Basket.API and Redis removes the basket store, so cart add/read/delete operations fail immediately. This exposes a confirmed availability weakness: no fallback or cached basket state exists.

Losing order-db connectivity makes order writes fail, turning checkout into 500s after retries in WebApp/BFF. It exposes missing graceful degradation or failover when the main order store is unreachable.

Loss of the PaymentProcessor to RabbitMQ message edge stalls payment result events, leaving orders permanently in payment processing state. This exposes missing dead-lettering or recovery for critical async payment messages.

If Ordering.API's outbound events are lost, downstream OrderProcessor never starts stock/order processing, halting the entire order pipeline. The failure shows how tightly the synchronous order path depends on the async bus.

Dropped HTTP requests from WebApp to Ordering.API silently lose order submissions unless the client retry succeeds. This can cause customer-facing order loss or duplicate submission if retry and idempotency are not correctly coordinated.

OrderProcessor cannot update order state when order-db is unreachable, stalling stock confirmations and payment transitions. It exposes missing recovery or dead-letter behavior for background order updates.

Latency on webapp to Basket.API propagates to every cart and checkout UI action, degrading the main purchasing flow. Without a tight timeout it can also exhaust WebApp HTTP connection pools under load.
High delay on catalog DB queries slows all product browsing from both WebApp and mobile BFF and may cause timeouts. This exposes the read-heavy catalog path to unbounded latency propagation.
Request loss from mobile BFF to Ordering.API makes order placement unavailable for mobile clients. It reveals the BFF has no fallback or queue when the order API becomes unreachable.
Loss of catalog API responses makes the storefront's product catalog unavailable, breaking browsing and search. This is a high-impact availability weakness in the primary user-facing read path.
